title: Four Americans Among Six Killed in Devastating Central Athens Explosion
snippet: A suspected gas explosion in a historic Athens neighborhood destroyed a residential building, killing six people, including two American couples visiting the Greek capital.
content:
ATHENS — A catastrophic explosion in the heart of Greece's capital has claimed the lives of six people, including four American tourists, local authorities confirmed Saturday. The blast completely leveled a two-story residential building in the historic Plaka district, a bustling neighborhood popular with travelers near the iconic Acropolis.

Tragedy Hits Visiting U.S. Couples

According to law enforcement sources and U.S. officials, the four American victims were two married couples staying in a short-term rental unit inside the building. Authorities were alerted when the group failed to show up for a 3:00 p.m. flight out of Athens International Airport on Friday.

Emergency crews wearing heavy protective gear deployed rescue dogs, acoustic sensors, and specialized search cameras to navigate the unstable pile of concrete and twisted metal. Rescue teams eventually recovered the bodies of the four Americans, along with an elderly Greek couple who lived in an adjacent apartment.

"I am deeply saddened to learn of the death of four American citizens in yesterday’s explosion in central Athens," U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle said in a statement posted on social media.

Gas Leak Suspected as Cause

Athens Mayor and local fire service officials indicated that the explosion was likely tied to municipal or residential gas infrastructure. Prior to the blast, several neighbors reported a distinct odor of gas in the area, which is lined with small hotels, private apartments, and vacation rentals.

The force of the detonation shattered windows and showered glass and masonry up to three blocks away, heavily damaging neighboring storefronts and parked vehicles. Arson and criminal investigation units from the Greek fire brigade remain on the scene to determine the exact origin of the leak and subsequent ignition.
